backlog.spec: In featurize, replace GetFingerprintAsNumPy with the count version (gen.GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy) so each bit holds how many times an environment occurs instead of 0/1. Keep radius 2 and 2048 bits and leave the RandomForest settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprints

backlog.spec: Compute the full RDKit 2D descriptor set (rdkit.Chem.Descriptors.CalcMolDescriptors) for each molecule, replace NaN and inf with 0, clip extreme values to the training 1st and 99th percentiles, and horizontally concatenate these with the Morgan fingerprint before fitting the random forest.
backlog.title: Add RDKit physchem descriptors

backlog.spec: Drop the fingerprint entirely and build features only from about 20 interpretable RDKit descriptors (MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, FractionCSP3, NumAromaticRings, RingCount, HeavyAtomCount, and similar). Fit the same random forest on these, since lipophilicity and polarity drive hepatic clearance.
backlog.title: Descriptors-only random forest

backlog.spec: Switch the Morgan generator to the feature-invariant variant (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator with atomInvariantsGenerator set to the feature invariants generator, or equivalently the useFeatures behaviour), keeping radius 2 and 2048 bits. This groups atoms by pharmacophoric role rather than exact element, which may generalise better across unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Feature-invariant Morgan (FCFP) fingerprints

backlog.spec: Replace the Morgan features with hashed atom-pair count fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, 2048 bits, count vector) and fit the same random forest. Atom pairs encode topological distances and are less tied to local ring environments than Morgan.
backlog.title: Atom-pair and torsion count fingerprints

backlog.spec: Featurize each molecule with the 167-bit MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys) instead of Morgan bits and fit the same random forest. MACCS is a compact, hand-curated key set and provides a different inductive bias for the ensemble.
backlog.title: MACCS structural keys

backlog.spec: Build features by concatenating Morgan count vectors at radius 1 (1024 bits) and radius 3 (2048 bits, hashed), so the model sees both local and wider environments. Keep the random forest unchanged.
backlog.title: Multi-scale Morgan concatenation

backlog.spec: Before fitting, convert train_y to its rank-based uniform quantiles (scipy.stats.rankdata divided by n) and train the random forest on those. Since the metric is Spearman correlation, this makes the regression focus on ordering and reduces the effect of extreme clearance values; predictions are returned on the transformed scale.
backlog.title: Rank-transform the target

backlog.spec: Clearance values are positive and right-skewed, so fit the model to log10 of the target (use np.log10 of np.clip(train_y, small_positive, None) to guard against zeros or negatives) and return the model predictions directly. Log scaling compresses the high tail that otherwise dominates squared-error splits.
backlog.title: Log-transform the target

backlog.spec: Replace the random forest with a LightGBM regressor (objective regression, num_leaves 31, learning_rate 0.03, 500 boosting rounds, feature_fraction 0.3, bagging_fraction 0.8 with bagging_freq 1, seed set from the seed argument). Use the same Morgan features as the baseline.
backlog.title: LightGBM on fingerprints and descriptors

backlog.spec: Replace the random forest with an XGBRegressor (max_depth 5, learning_rate 0.05, n_estimators 400, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.5, random_state=seed, tree_method hist) fitted on the Morgan bit features. Gradient boosting usually beats bagged trees on sparse fingerprints when tuned for shallow depth.
backlog.title: XGBoost gradient boosting

backlog.spec: Fit a CatBoostRegressor (depth 6, iterations 800, learning_rate 0.05, loss_function RMSE, random_seed=seed, verbose False) on the Morgan features. CatBoost's ordered boosting and symmetric trees are often more robust than standard boosting on small datasets, so it is a good ensemble candidate.
backlog.title: CatBoost regressor

backlog.spec: Compute the Tanimoto (Jaccard on binary Morgan bits) similarity matrix between train and test molecules, that is K = (A·B) / (|A| + |B| - A·B) with numpy, and fit sklearn SVR with kernel='precomputed' (C about 10, epsilon 0.1). Chemical similarity kernels are a strong baseline for molecular property prediction.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-kernel support vector regression

backlog.spec: Build the Tanimoto similarity matrix on binary Morgan fingerprints as K = (A·B)/(|A|+|B|-A·B). Fit sklearn KernelRidge with kernel='precomputed' and alpha about 0.5 on the training targets, then predict test values from the test-to-train kernel. This is a smooth, similarity-based regressor with no tree structure.
backlog.title: Kernel ridge with Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Compute Tanimoto similarities between test and training molecules on Morgan bits. For each test molecule take the k=10 most similar training molecules and predict the similarity-weighted average of their targets, with weights = similarity raised to power 3 to emphasise close analogues. Return these as predictions.
backlog.title: Similarity-weighted k-nearest-neighbour

backlog.spec: Train the baseline random forest and a LightGBM regressor on the same Morgan features, convert each model's test predictions to ranks, and return the average of the two rank vectors scaled to [0,1]. Averaging ranks removes scale differences between the models and suits a Spearman-based score.
backlog.title: Rank-averaged ensemble of RF and boosting

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, split the training data into 4 inner folds grouped by Murcko scaffold. Get out-of-fold predictions from a random forest, a kernel ridge model on Tanimoto similarity and a LightGBM model. Fit a non-negative linear regression (scipy.optimize.nnls) on those out-of-fold predictions and apply the learned weights to the models refit on all training data.
backlog.title: Stacked ensemble with inner cross-validation

backlog.spec: Increase min_samples_leaf from 1 to 5 and keep max_features at 0.3 and 300 trees. Larger leaves smooth the predictions and reduce overfitting to individual scaffolds in the held-out folds.
backlog.title: Random forest with larger leaves for smoother predictions

backlog.spec: Set RandomForestRegressor's max_samples to 0.5 (each tree sees half the training set, drawn without replacement via bootstrap=True and max_samples=0.5). This adds diversity between trees and acts as regularisation on the correlated training molecules.
backlog.title: Subsampled bootstrap in the forest

backlog.spec: Compute the Murcko scaffold of every training molecule and count how many training molecules share each scaffold. Give each training molecule a sample weight equal to 1 divided by its scaffold count (normalised to mean 1), and pass these weights to RandomForestRegressor.fit via sample_weight. This stops over-represented scaffold families from dominating the fit.
backlog.title: Scaffold-frequency sample weighting

backlog.spec: After featurizing the training set, drop every fingerprint column that is set in fewer than 3 training molecules (or in all of them), and apply the same column mask to the test features. Fewer, more informative features reduce noise for the random forest's random feature selection.
backlog.title: Remove near-constant fingerprint bits

backlog.spec: Train one random forest on Morgan radius-2 bits, one on atom-pair counts and one on MACCS keys, each with the same random forest settings and seed. Average their test predictions. Different fingerprints capture different structural information, so the average should reduce variance.
backlog.title: Ensemble over several fingerprint types

backlog.spec: Fit sklearn GradientBoostingRegressor with loss='huber' (alpha 0.9), n_estimators 400, learning_rate 0.05, max_depth 4, subsample 0.8, random_state=seed on Morgan count features. The Huber loss is robust to outlying clearance measurements in the training targets.
backlog.title: Gradient boosting with Huber loss

backlog.spec: Hold out a random 15 percent of the training molecules, grouped by Murcko scaffold, as an inner validation set. Train LightGBM with up to 2000 rounds and learning_rate 0.02, stopping when the validation L2 loss has not improved for 100 rounds. Then refit on all training data using the best round count found.
backlog.title: LightGBM with early stopping on an inner split

backlog.spec: Train LightGBM with a learning-rate schedule that starts at 0.1 and decays geometrically to 0.01 over 800 rounds, implemented with the callback reset_parameter in lightgbm.train, keeping num_leaves 15 and feature_fraction 0.3. A decaying schedule usually gives better generalisation than a fixed rate.
backlog.title: Decaying learning-rate boosting

backlog.spec: Use sklearn MLPRegressor on the Morgan bit features with hidden_layer_sizes (512, 128), activation relu, solver adam, learning_rate_init 1e-3, alpha 1e-2 (L2 weight decay), early_stopping True with validation_fraction 0.15, max_iter 300, random_state=seed. Standardise the targets with mean and std from the training data and invert the transform on the output.
backlog.title: Multilayer perceptron on fingerprints with weight decay

backlog.spec: Replace the regression target with a pairwise ranking objective, since the metric is Spearman. In fit_predict, build the Morgan, atom-pair and MACCS feature matrices as before. Sample about 50 random pairs (i, j) per training molecule with y_i != y_j, and form difference vectors x_i - x_j with label 1 if y_i > y_j, else 0 (mirror the pairs to keep the classes balanced). Fit a LightGBM or logistic-regression classifier on these differences with no intercept, using the seed. Score each test molecule with its linear score w.x (or with the mean classifier output against a sample of training molecules for the tree version). Average the scores from the three feature sets after converting each to ranks. Keep the rank-transformed forests as a fallback if the pair count is too small.
backlog.title: Pairwise ranking model on fingerprint differences

backlog.spec: Augment the data at the string level. For each training molecule, generate K=8 randomized SMILES with Chem.MolToSmiles(mol, doRandom=True, canonical=False), using a seeded random generator (RDKit random seed set from the seed argument). Repeat the training label for every variant, then fit the three-forest ensemble on the enlarged set. At prediction time, also generate K randomized SMILES for each test molecule and average the predictions across the variants before the ensemble mean. Keep the target rank transform. Cap the total training rows so that the 15 fits stay well under the 10-minute limit, for example by setting K to 4 if needed.
backlog.title: Randomized-SMILES augmentation with test-time averaging

backlog.spec: Use the unlabeled test molecules in the fit, as allowed inside fit_predict. Round 1: fit the rank-target three-forest ensemble on the training molecules and predict the test set. Keep the 30 percent of test molecules whose three forest predictions have the lowest spread (most agreement) or whose predictions are most extreme in rank, and add them to the training set with their predicted rank as the label. Round 2: refit the same ensemble on the augmented set and output its test predictions. Use only the seed for randomness. This is a single extra round, so runtime roughly doubles, which fits the budget.
backlog.title: Transductive self-training with confident test pseudo-labels

backlog.spec: Swap the RandomForestRegressor for sklearn ExtraTreesRegressor for the Morgan member only, keeping the atom-pair and MACCS forests unchanged. Use n_estimators=N_TREES, max_features=0.3 (the same setting), min_samples_leaf=1, bootstrap=False (the ExtraTrees default), n_jobs=-1, random_state=seed. Extra trees choose split thresholds at random, so they add a different kind of variance to the ensemble. Keep the rank-transformed target. Average the three member predictions as before. Only this one member changes, so the diff is small.
backlog.title: ExtraTrees member in place of the Morgan random forest

backlog.spec: Change how the forest samples its training rows so that bootstraps resample Murcko scaffold groups instead of single molecules. In fit_predict, compute the Bemis-Murcko scaffold (MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles) for each training molecule and group the rows by scaffold. Train each tree on its own bootstrap that draws scaffold groups with replacement and includes all molecules of each drawn group. Implement this by fitting many small RandomForest or DecisionTree models (for example 300 trees) on separate scaffold-bootstrap row sets, using the seed to draw them, and averaging their predictions. Keep the rank target and the three feature sets. The aim is trees that see different skeletons, which matches the test protocol.
backlog.title: Scaffold-cluster bootstrap for each tree

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform rank target with normal scores. Compute r = rankdata(train_y) and set y = scipy.stats.norm.ppf((r - 0.5) / n), so the target is Gaussian-shaped with the tails spread out. Use this target for all three random forests, keeping the rest of the script unchanged. The change alters how the trees weight the extreme molecules versus the bulk, while the Spearman metric still depends only on the ordering of the predictions. Compare with the uniform rank target as a single change.
backlog.title: Gaussian-rank (normal-score) target transform

backlog.spec: Reweight training molecules so that the rank-target distribution is flattened. Compute the rank target y as before. Estimate local density by binning y into 10 equal-width bins and set each sample weight to 1 divided by its bin count, normalized to mean 1. Pass these weights as sample_weight to RandomForestRegressor.fit for all three forests. This keeps sparse extreme regions from being swamped by the dense middle, which often helps when rank error is concentrated at the ends. Leave the features and hyperparameters unchanged.
backlog.title: Density-balanced sample weights on the rank target

backlog.spec: Add a new feature family built from RDKit's topological descriptors that differ from the Morgan bits. For each molecule compute rdMolDescriptors.CalcAUTOCORR2D (192 values) and the BCUT2D descriptors from rdMolDescriptors.BCUT2D (8 values from Gasteiger-charged atoms, with NaNs replaced by 0). Concatenate them into one dense array. Fit a fourth random forest on this descriptor array, using the same rank target and seed, and add its predictions to the ensemble mean with the other three members. Keep the existing three members as they are. The descriptors are continuous, so a forest with max_features=0.3 uses them differently from the bit-based members.
backlog.title: Autocorrelation and BCUT descriptor features

backlog.spec: Let the data pick the forest's feature-subsampling setting inside each fit. For each feature set, fit RandomForestRegressor with oob_score=True for max_features in {0.1, 0.3, 0.6} (set n_estimators to a smaller value such as 150 to keep runtime in budget), using the rank target and the seed. Compute the out-of-bag Spearman correlation between the OOB predictions and the training rank target. Refit the forest with the best setting and the full N_TREES, then use it for prediction. Each feature set keeps its own choice. Do not use the test molecules for selection.
backlog.title: Per-fit selection of forest max_features by out-of-bag score

backlog.spec: Add a second stage that corrects the forest ensemble. Compute out-of-fold forest predictions on the training molecules with a 5-fold KFold inside fit_predict (using the seed for the split), giving a first-stage prediction for each training molecule. Compute residuals r = rank target minus out-of-fold prediction. Fit a small, shrunk gradient-boosting model (sklearn GradientBoostingRegressor with n_estimators=100, learning_rate=0.05, max_depth=3, subsample=0.8) on the Morgan-plus-descriptor features to predict r. For test molecules, add the shrinkage-scaled second-stage prediction (multiply by 0.5) to the first-stage ensemble mean. Keep the first stage unchanged.
backlog.title: Residual boosting on top of the forest ensemble

backlog.spec: In featurize(), before computing any fingerprint or descriptor, standardize each SMILES: parse it, keep only the largest covalent fragment (drop counterions and salts), neutralize charges with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger, and canonicalize tautomers with rdMolStandardize.TautomerEnumerator (or skip tautomers if it is slow). Fall back to the raw molecule if standardization raises or returns None. Keep the three-forest ensemble, rank target and all other settings unchanged. Only the input molecules change.
backlog.title: Standardize molecules before featurizing

backlog.spec: Add a fourth feature block computed from a single 3D conformer per molecule: embed with rdDistGeom.ETKDGv3 (fixed random seed, 1 conformer, fall back to 2D-only zeros if embedding fails), then compute rdMolDescriptors.CalcPMI1/2/3, CalcNPR1/2, CalcPBF, CalcRDF (or the MORSE and WHIM descriptors if available) and concatenate them. Train one additional random forest on this block alone (max_features 0.3, 300 trees, rank target) and add its prediction to the averaged members. Leave the existing Morgan, atom-pair and MACCS forests as they are.
backlog.title: 3D shape descriptors from one embedded conformer

backlog.spec: Replace the regression forests for the Morgan member with an ordinal model. Convert the rank target y in (0,1) into K-1 = 9 binary labels, one per threshold t_k at the deciles of y, where label_k = (y > t_k). Fit one RandomForestClassifier per threshold on the same Morgan features (300 trees, max_features 0.3, seeded, n_jobs=-1). For each test molecule the prediction is the mean over thresholds of P(y > t_k), which is a monotone-consistent expected rank. Average this with the existing two member predictions as before.
backlog.title: Ordinal threshold decomposition of the rank target

backlog.spec: Before fitting each forest, augment the training set with synthetic molecules. For each feature set, draw about as many new pairs as there are training rows, using a Beta(0.4, 0.4) mixing weight lambda seeded from the seed argument. Build each synthetic row as lambda*x_i + (1-lambda)*x_j and its target as lambda*y_i + (1-lambda)*y_j on the rank scale, with i and j drawn at random from the training set. Fit the forest on the original plus augmented rows (so about twice the data) and predict test rows unchanged. Keep the rest of the pipeline the same.
backlog.title: Mixup augmentation in fingerprint space

backlog.spec: After the ensemble produces test predictions, refine them using test-test similarity. Compute Morgan (radius 2, 2048-bit) Tanimoto similarities among the test molecules only. For each test molecule, replace its prediction with a weighted average of its own prediction and those of test neighbours with Tanimoto similarity above 0.6, using weights equal to the similarity (self weight 1). Molecules with no such neighbour keep their original prediction. Training is unchanged. This uses only the test SMILES and needs no labels.
backlog.title: Transductive smoothing across similar test molecules

backlog.spec: Add a fourth member that uses the forest's own similarity. Fit one RandomForestRegressor on the Morgan features with min_samples_leaf=5 and 500 trees, then compute, for each test molecule, the leaf-co-occurrence proximity to every training molecule using model.apply() (proximity = fraction of trees in which the two share a leaf). Take the 15 training molecules with highest proximity and predict the proximity-weighted mean of their rank targets. Average this prediction with the three existing members. The proximity weighting is computed only from leaves, so no new features are needed.
backlog.title: Random-forest proximity kNN regressor as an extra member

backlog.spec: Change only how member predictions are combined. Each member (the three forests) produces a vector of test predictions. Convert each member's test vector to ranks within the test set (scipy rankdata divided by the number of test molecules), then average those rank vectors across members and return the average. Training is unchanged. This makes each member count equally regardless of its prediction spread, and since the metric is Spearman it matches the metric's scale.
backlog.title: Rank-average the member outputs instead of the mean

backlog.spec: Reduce variance of each member by averaging over several forests trained with different random states. For each of the three feature sets, fit 3 RandomForestRegressor models with random_state set to seed, seed+1000, seed+2000 (same 300 trees each, max_features 0.3, rank target), average their predictions, then average the three feature-set results as before. The total tree count per member becomes 900. Keep all other settings unchanged, and watch the runtime stays well under 10 minutes for 15 fits.
backlog.title: Repeated seeded forests inside each member to cut variance

backlog.spec: Make the number of trees per member adaptive. Fit each forest with warm_start=True in increments of 50 trees, starting at 50 and up to 600. After each increment, record the out-of-bag R-squared (set oob_score=True) on the rank target. Stop growing when the OOB score has improved by less than 0.002 for two consecutive increments, and use the tree count at which the score peaked. Apply this separately to each of the three feature sets, so the members may use different numbers of trees. The seed argument drives all randomness.
backlog.title: Stop growing each forest once its out-of-bag score plateaus

backlog.spec: Clean the training labels before fitting. Within fit_predict, compute the Morgan Tanimoto similarity matrix among the training molecules, and for each training molecule take the mean rank target of its 5 most similar other training molecules. Remove the 5% of training molecules whose rank target differs most from that neighbour mean (the likely noisy measurements), then fit all three forests on the remaining molecules. Test molecules are predicted as before. The cleaning uses only training labels, and the threshold is a fixed fraction, not a tuned value.
backlog.title: Drop training molecules that disagree with their fingerprint neighbours

backlog.spec: Wrap the existing three-forest ensemble in an outer bag. For b in range(8), draw a seeded random 75% subset of the training molecules without replacement (rng = np.random.default_rng(seed + b)), fit the three forests on that subset with N_TREES=150 each, predict the test molecules, and store the predictions. Return the mean over the 8 bags of the mean over the three forests. Keep the rank-transformed target. Estimated cost is about 16 s per fit, which fits the 10-minute limit for 15 fits.
backlog.title: Subbagging the whole ensemble over molecules

backlog.spec: Add a fourth ensemble member on Extended Reduced Graph fingerprints. Compute rdReducedGraphs.GetErGFingerprint(mol) for each molecule (it returns a float vector of about 315 values), stack the results into a matrix, and fit a RandomForestRegressor with the same settings (N_TREES, MAX_FEATURES, MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF, random_state=seed) on the rank target. Average its test predictions into the existing mean with equal weight. Skip the member and fall back to the current ensemble if the import fails.
backlog.title: ErG reduced-graph fingerprint member

backlog.spec: Add a fourth ensemble member on 2D pharmacophore pair fingerprints. Use rdkit.Chem.Pharm2D.Gobbi_Pharm2D.factory with rdkit.Chem.Pharm2D.Generate.Gen2DFingerprint for each molecule, convert the bit vector to a numpy array, and reduce it to a fixed width of 2048 by folding the indices modulo 2048 with OR. Fit a RandomForestRegressor with the same settings as the existing members on the rank target. Add its test predictions to the mean with equal weight.
backlog.title: Gobbi 2D pharmacophore fingerprint member

backlog.spec: Add a fourth ensemble member on Avalon fingerprints. Use rdkit.Avalon.pyAvalonTools.GetAvalonFP(mol, nBits=1024) for each molecule and convert it to a numpy array. Fit a RandomForestRegressor with the existing settings on the rank target and average its test predictions into the ensemble with equal weight to the other members. Avalon uses a different hashing path from Morgan, so the member adds a structurally different view.
backlog.title: Avalon fingerprint member

backlog.spec: Denoise the training labels before fitting. Compute the rank target y as now. Within the training fold only, compute the Tanimoto similarity matrix on binary Morgan fingerprints (radius 2, 2048 bits). For each training molecule, take the mean y of its 5 nearest other training molecules, and set y_smooth = 0.5 * y + 0.5 * neighbour_mean. Fit all forests on y_smooth and leave the prediction code unchanged. The training labels are never used at test time except through the fitted model.
backlog.title: Neighbour-smoothed training targets

backlog.spec: Add a linear member that the forests cannot replicate. Build log1p count Morgan fingerprints at radii 1, 2 and 3 (2048 bits each), concatenate them, and standardize the columns using the training fold statistics. Fit sklearn RidgeCV with alphas logspace(-1, 4, 12) on the rank target, using the default efficient leave-one-out selection. Average its test predictions with the forest ensemble using the same equal weight as the other members.
backlog.title: Ridge member on log-count Morgan fingerprints

backlog.spec: Add a gradient-boosting member on about 20 RDKit descriptors (MolWt, MolLogP, TPSA, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, NumAromaticRings, FractionCSP3, RingCount, HeavyAtomCount, and similar). Use sklearn HistGradientBoostingRegressor with monotonic_cst set to +1 for MolLogP and 0 for every other column, max_iter=300, learning_rate=0.05, max_leaf_nodes=15, l2_regularization=1.0, and random_state=seed. Fit on the rank target. Use the monotone prior that higher lipophilicity should not lower predicted clearance. Average its test predictions with the forest ensemble.
backlog.title: Monotone-constrained boosting on physicochemical descriptors

backlog.spec: Use the unlabeled test molecules when building the feature space. Stack the binary Morgan fingerprints of the training and test molecules, drop bits set in fewer than 2 molecules of the stacked matrix, then fit sklearn TruncatedSVD with 64 components and random_state=seed on the stacked matrix. Append the 64 SVD scores to each molecule's existing features for the Morgan forest only. The fit uses no labels, so it is legal under the harness, and it adds a dense, smoothed view of chemical space.
backlog.title: Transductive unsupervised feature space

backlog.spec: Replace the equal mean over members with learned weights. Inside fit_predict, run an inner 3-fold split of the training molecules (seeded KFold) and produce out-of-fold rank predictions for each member. Search a simplex grid of member weights in steps of 0.1 and keep the weights that maximize the mean Spearman correlation with the true training ranks across the inner folds. Refit each member on the full training fold and combine the test predictions with those weights. No extra learners are added, so the change is only a weighting step.
backlog.title: Member weights learned on the training fold

backlog.spec: Shrink predictions for molecules that look unlike the training set. For each test molecule, compute its maximum Tanimoto similarity to any training molecule on binary Morgan fingerprints (radius 2, 2048 bits). Let s be that similarity, and set w = clip((s - 0.3) / 0.4, 0, 1). Return pred_final = w * ensemble_pred + (1 - w) * 0.5, where 0.5 is the mean rank target. Low-similarity molecules are then pulled toward the middle, so the ranking expresses less confidence on them. Tune the 0.3 and 0.7 anchors only through the single allowed job.
backlog.title: Applicability-domain shrinkage toward the mean

backlog.spec: In each RandomForestRegressor member, replace model.predict(X) with the median of the per-tree predictions: stack [t.predict(X) for t in model.estimators_] into an array of shape (n_trees, n_test) and take np.median over axis 0. Keep everything else (three feature sets, rank target, mean across members) unchanged. This is a robust leaf-value aggregation that does not change how trees are grown.
backlog.title: Median aggregation across trees instead of mean

backlog.spec: Add a feature set for each molecule built from its Bemis-Murcko decomposition. Compute the Murcko scaffold with MurckoScaffold.GetScaffoldForMol and atom-level scaffold membership. Build two 1024-bit Morgan count vectors (radius 2): one from environments centred on scaffold atoms, one from environments centred on side-chain atoms. Concatenate them and train a fourth RandomForest member on them, averaged into the ensemble with the existing members. Use the same seed and rank target.
backlog.title: Scaffold-versus-side-chain Morgan split features

backlog.spec: Add a fragment-based feature set. For each molecule, run rdkit.Chem.BRICS.BRICSDecompose to get a set of fragment SMILES. Hash each fragment SMILES into a fixed 1024-slot vector with a stable hash (e.g. zlib.crc32 modulo 1024) and count occurrences. Fit one RandomForest on these counts with the same settings and rank target, and average its prediction into the ensemble with the other members.
backlog.title: BRICS fragment-count member

backlog.spec: Before fitting each member, train a quick classifier (RandomForestClassifier, 100 trees, seeded) to distinguish training fingerprints from test fingerprints (Morgan bits). Take each training molecule's predicted probability of being a test molecule p, and set its sample_weight to p/(1-p), clipped to [0.2, 5] and normalised to mean 1. Pass these weights as sample_weight to each member's fit so that training molecules that look like the test set count more.
backlog.title: Adversarial-validation importance weights

backlog.spec: Before fitting each member, duplicate the training fingerprint matrix three times. In each copy, set a random 20 percent of the 1-bits to 0 using a numpy RandomState seeded from the seed argument. Stack the original and the copies, repeat the rank targets three times to match, fit the forest on the stacked data, and predict on the unmodified test fingerprints. This regularises the forest against brittle single-bit splits.
backlog.title: Random bit-dropout augmentation of training fingerprints

backlog.spec: Instead of one global model per member, fit a small local model for each test molecule. Compute Tanimoto similarity between each test molecule's Morgan bit vector and all training molecules, take its k=150 nearest training molecules, and fit a RandomForestRegressor (60 trees, max_features 0.3, seeded) on just those rows and their rank targets. Predict that test molecule with its local model. Keep the global three-member average as a fallback for test molecules whose top-k mean similarity is below 0.2.
backlog.title: Local neighbourhood forests at prediction time

backlog.spec: Train the same forest setup on three different targets: the uniform rank of y, the standardised raw y (z-score, clipped at plus or minus 3), and the rank of log10 of the raw y. Each target gets its own RandomForest on the Morgan features. Convert each set of test predictions to ranks with scipy rankdata and average the three rank vectors. Output the averaged ranks divided by the number of test molecules. This hedges the choice of target transform, which earlier single-target tests showed matters.
backlog.title: Ensemble over target transforms

backlog.spec: Replace the single max_features setting with a schedule across forests. Build four RandomForestRegressor models per feature set, each with 75 trees, and assign them max_features values 0.05, 0.15, 0.3 and 0.6 in a fixed order. Each forest uses its own seed derived from the seed argument. Average the four forests' predictions within each feature set before the cross-feature-set mean. The mix of feature-subspace sizes covers both sparse-signal and dense-signal regimes without tuning one value.
backlog.title: Cycling forest feature-fraction schedule

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, before the final fit, evaluate a small grid of featurization settings with an inner grouped split of the training data: Morgan radius in {1, 2, 3} and fpSize in {1024, 2048}, plus atom-pair and MACCS as fixed options. Use the Murcko scaffold of each molecule as the group label and a 3-fold GroupKFold. Score each option by the Spearman correlation of its out-of-fold predictions with the training targets, keep the best two options, and average those two members for the final prediction. Keep the total inner work under the job time limit by using 100 trees per forest.
backlog.title: Evolutionary search over featurization hyperparameters per fit

backlog.spec: For each member, fit a RandomForestRegressor on the rank targets and read its out-of-bag predictions (oob_prediction_, with bootstrap=True and oob_score=True). Build new targets as 0.7 times the original rank target plus 0.3 times the OOB prediction, rescaled to [0, 1]. Refit a second forest of the same settings on the new targets, and use that second forest's test predictions in the mean ensemble. The blend shrinks noisy labels toward what the model can explain.
backlog.title: Self-distilled soft targets from out-of-bag predictions

backlog.spec: Add a small hand-written set of about 20 SMARTS patterns for known hepatic metabolic soft spots: O-methyl and N-methyl groups, benzylic CH2 and CH3, aromatic CH positions adjacent to heteroatoms, tertiary amines, esters, amides, thioethers, unsubstituted phenyl rings, and terminal alkenes. For each molecule, count matches per pattern with rdkit Chem.MolFromSmarts and GetSubstructMatches. Append these counts, plus Crippen logP, TPSA, MW and HBD/HBA from rdkit.Chem.Descriptors, as an extra feature block. Fit one RandomForestRegressor on this block (same settings as the other members) and add it as a fifth member of the mean ensemble. Use only the training fold to define anything data-dependent; the SMARTS list is fixed.
backlog.title: Metabolic-liability SMARTS counts

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, compute a per-bit target encoding from the training fold only. For each of the 2048 Morgan bits, take the mean rank target of training molecules that have the bit set, shrunk toward the global mean with prior weight 5 (smoothed mean = (sum + 5*global) / (count + 5)). Use inner 5-fold out-of-fold encoding for the training rows so a molecule never sees its own label, and full-training encoding for test rows. Each molecule's feature vector becomes the average of its set bits' encodings plus min and max over its set bits. Fit a RandomForestRegressor on these 3 summary features concatenated with the raw Morgan bits, and add it as an extra ensemble member.
backlog.title: Bayesian target encoding of Morgan bits

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, run k-means (k=4, seeded) on the training Morgan bit vectors to split training molecules into 4 clusters. Train one RandomForestRegressor (150 trees, same max_features) per cluster, plus one global forest on all training molecules. For each test molecule, assign it a weight over clusters from its Tanimoto similarity to each cluster centroid (softmax with temperature 0.1 on the similarities). The prediction is the weighted sum of cluster-forest predictions, averaged 50/50 with the global forest prediction. Each cluster forest sees only its own molecules, so it specializes to a chemical region.
backlog.title: Scaffold-cluster expert forests

backlog.spec: Replace each feature-set member (Morgan, atom-pair, MACCS, Gobbi) with four RandomForestRegressors of 75 trees each, using different seeds (seed, seed+1, seed+2, seed+3) and max_features 0.3, and average them within the member. Then add one XGBRegressor (max_depth 5, learning_rate 0.05, 400 estimators, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.5, random_state=seed) fit on the concatenated Morgan and MACCS bits, and average it into the final ensemble with weight equal to one member. Keep the rank-transformed target. This combines the best-scoring bagging change with the boosting member that scored well on its own.
backlog.title: Retry bagged forests with XGBoost member

backlog.spec: Replace the mean of each forest's predictions with a conditional median. For each feature-set forest, fit as usual on the rank target. For a test molecule, call model.apply on the training matrix and on the test matrix to get leaf ids. For each tree, the training molecules sharing the test molecule's leaf get weight 1 divided by the leaf size. Sum these weights over trees to get a weight per training molecule, normalize, and take the weighted median of the training rank targets. Use this weighted median as that member's prediction, then average the members as before. This gives a robust conditional-median estimate rather than a leaf-mean.
backlog.title: Quantile regression forest median

backlog.spec: Before fitting, fold each 2048-bit Morgan and atom-pair fingerprint down to 512 columns by OR-ing the four 512-bit blocks together (column j = bit j OR bit j+512 OR bit j+1024 OR bit j+1536). This is deterministic and needs no training data, so it is consistent across folds. Use the folded matrices in the Morgan and atom-pair members, keep the MACCS and Gobbi members unchanged, and leave all other settings as they are. The aim is less noise per split, since the fold merges bits that collide across features.
backlog.title: Bit-OR folding of fingerprints

backlog.spec: Add a feature block describing ring topology, computed with rdkit ring info. Count ring systems (groups of fused or spiro rings), the number of rings in each system, the largest ring-system size in atoms, the number of aromatic and aliphatic rings, the number of fused-ring bonds, counts of ring sizes 3 through 8, and the fraction of heavy atoms in rings. Compute these per molecule with no training-set statistics. Fit a RandomForestRegressor on this block alone and add it as an extra member of the mean ensemble, using the same tree and feature settings as the other members.
backlog.title: Ring-system topology features

backlog.spec: Keep the rank-uniform target but clip it before fitting. Replace each training rank value r with min(max(r, 0.05), 0.95), so the most extreme 5 percent at each end share their boundary value. This removes the leverage of extreme measured clearance values that are often assay noise, while keeping the order of the middle 90 percent unchanged. Leave the featurization, forests and ensembling exactly as in the incumbent. Only the target changes.
backlog.title: Winsorized rank target

backlog.spec: Fit each feature-set RandomForestRegressor as a multi-output model whose target matrix has four columns: the rank target plus three auxiliary columns, namely Crippen logP, TPSA and molecular weight, each standardized on the training fold. RandomForestRegressor supports multi-output natively, so one call fits all columns. The tree splits are then driven partly by physicochemical structure, which may regularize the rank-target splits. Use only the first column (the rank target) for prediction, and average the members as in the incumbent. The auxiliary weight can be scaled with a column multiplier of 0.5.
backlog.title: Multi-output forest with physchem auxiliary targets

backlog.spec: Before each forest fit, build a random 50 percent column mask for each tree rather than relying only on max_features. Implement this by fitting 300 DecisionTreeRegressor instances, each trained with max_features 0.3 on its own bootstrap sample of molecules and a random subset of half of the feature columns chosen with rng=seed. Keep the same members and ensemble. Average the trees' predictions. This is a tree-level dropout, a stronger column-level regularizer than the forest's per-split sampling, and it may lower variance on scaffold-held-out folds.
backlog.title: Dropout-style feature masking during forest fitting

incumbent.description: Adds a fourth ensemble member: a RandomForestRegressor on Gobbi 2D pharmacophore pair fingerprints, folded to 2048 bits by OR over indices modulo 2048, fit on the rank target and averaged with equal weight.

memo:
Helped: ensembling per-feature-set random forests (slot 0, 0.5635 vs 0.6103 baseline), rank-transforming the target (slot 1, 0.5266), and adding a Gobbi 2D pharmacophore forest as a fourth member (slot 25, 0.5000, incumbent). Dropping the Morgan forest hurt (slot 4, +0.0192).

Did not help: CatBoost (slot 2), min_samples_leaf 5 (slot 8), log10 target (slot 13), descriptors-only models (slots 7 and 29), pairwise ranking (slot 9), stacking (slot 23), in-fit featurization search (slot 27, 0.5721). Fifth members on top of the incumbent (slots 30, 31) and a proximity-kNN member (slot 28) were worse. Multi-output targets (slot 32) were also worse (+0.0100). Within noise (sd about 0.0070): Morgan counts, LightGBM, FCFP, kernel ridge, XGBoost swap, standardization.

Next: retry slot 26's bagging (four 75-tree forests per feature set, 0.4962) on the incumbent, perhaps with XGBoost. Try other diverse pharmacophore or topological fingerprint forests as replacements, not extra members. Treat gains under 0.007 as noise.
